beats.intent: ThinkSR addresses a mismatch between compact thought and dense super-resolution output.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The central problem is that compact reasoning has to produce detail at every spatial position.

params.headline: Compact thought must produce a dense image field
params.sub: A CTM-style process adapted for super-resolution.

beats.intent: The baseline issue is a representation mismatch, not just a scoring problem.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The compact representation is efficient, but super-resolution asks for structure spread across the whole image. A window-wise adaptation makes the spatial demand explicit. DQ-CTM is framed as the version built for that dense output.

params.headline: Compact state and dense output pull in different directions
params.note: Figure 1 compares CTM, a window-wise adaptation, and DQ-CTM.

beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a persistent dense carrier that a compact thought process can repeatedly read and update.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps a dense carrier alive instead of asking a compact state to hold the whole image. The encoder creates the carrier used by the later process. Windowing exposes local fields for thought updates. Shared DQ-CTM ticks repeatedly read and update those windows. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the high-resolution output.

params.headline: A dense carrier is updated by compact thought

beats.intent: The dense carrier is encoded from the low-resolution image, then partitioned into windows.
beats.narration: The equation defines the handoff from image input to windowed carrier. The low-resolution image is the starting signal. The encoder maps that image into dense features. The windowing operator partitions those features. The resulting windows are the units passed onward.

terms.label: the encoder that builds dense features
the windowing operation on those features

beats.intent: The end-to-end system connects encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder as one reconstruction path.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The architecture makes the carrier visible as the object that survives through the method. Encoding starts the path from the low-resolution image. Windowing gives the compact thought process local material to operate on. Shared ticks reuse the same DQ-CTM process across updates. Decoding produces the final reconstruction.

params.headline: The carrier persists through the reconstruction path

beats.intent: Reconstruction changes over ticks from T=0 through T=4 and is compared with bicubic and ground truth.
beats.claim: Reconstruction at T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.narration: The reconstruction figure shows the iterative output rather than a single final image. The zero-tick state anchors the starting reconstruction. Later ticks show how the output changes through time. Bicubic gives the simple interpolation reference. Ground truth gives the target the reconstruction is judged against.

params.headline: The reconstruction is shown across T=0 to T=4

beats.intent: Absolute-error maps compare the same crops using one shared colour scale.
beats.claim: Absolute-error maps on the same crops, one shared colour scale.
beats.narration: The error maps move the comparison from appearance to pixel-level error. Using the same crops keeps the locations comparable. A shared colour scale makes error magnitude comparable across methods. The figure is therefore about relative error patterns on identical examples.

params.headline: The same crops share one error scale

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with CNN baselines but trails recent lightweight transformers.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The benchmark places DQ-CTM-SR among lightweight super-resolution methods. CNN baselines sit near the same average score range. CATANet is the recent lightweight transformer reference and scores higher. DQ-CTM-SR uses more parameters than CATANet in this table.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is competitive but not best
params.note: Table 1 reports x4 average over five benchmarks.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is smaller than CARN but larger than the other listed lightweight baselines.
beats.narration: Parameter count gives the cost side of the comparison. CARN is the largest method listed. DQ-CTM-SR is smaller than CARN. IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet all use fewer parameters than DQ-CTM-SR. The table does not present DQ-CTM-SR as the smallest model.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest listed model

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR narrowly exceeds CARN and IMDN on average, trails RFDN slightly, and trails CATANet clearly.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: Average score gives the quality side of the comparison. CATANet has the highest reported average. RFDN is slightly ahead of DQ-CTM-SR. DQ-CTM-SR is just above CARN and IMDN. The result supports competitiveness, but not leadership.

beats.intent: ThinkSR’s contribution is the dense carrier that lets compact thought operate in a super-resolution pipeline.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The main idea is architectural: keep the dense field persistent while compact thought updates it. The reported result is competitive with CNN baselines. The same result remains behind recent lightweight transformers.

params.headline: The dense carrier is the core contribution
